name: Miro
tagline: Online collaborative whiteboard for diagrams, workshops, and planning

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Starter listed at $10/member/month monthly and $8/member/month annually.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited members and boards, but only the 3 most recently created boards remain editable; 10 AI credits/month; 100 MCP calls/day
tiers.notes: No guest or visitor roles; Free-team boards are visible to all team members by default.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Unlimited private boards and project spaces; visitor editing; 25 AI credits/member/month; 500 MCP calls/day

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited workspaces and guests; 50 AI credits/member/month; 2,000 MCP calls/day; SSO, advanced diagramming and two-way integrations

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 30-member minimum; starts at 2,500 pooled AI credits/month; 10,000 MCP calls/day; SCIM, data residency and organization governance

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited members and boards, but only 3 most recent boards editable; 10 AI credits/month and 100 MCP calls/day; no guests or visitors
pricing.billingTerms: free + per-member monthly or annual billing; annual saves 20% and is prepaid; automated card billing has no seat minimum, while invoicing is annual-only with 10 Starter or 5 Business licenses
pricing.hiddenCosts: New paid members are prorated immediately, while removed seats stay billable until renewal; extra AI-credit packs, Enterprise Guard and Premium Support cost extra; some data-residency migrations carry fees

verdictSummary: A simple multiplayer whiteboard is doable; Miro's value is scale, templates, integrations, facilitation, permissions, and reliability with many users.
coreLoopDIY: Build a canvas with sticky notes, shapes, connectors, comments, and optional multiplayer sync.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for workshops where dozens of people can join and everything still works.

priorArt.name: tldraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source canvas/whiteboard SDK and app; excellent prior art for DIY whiteboards.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: An integrated canvas, docs, databases, and planning workspace for teams willing to accept a younger product and real self-hosting chores.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.engines: Self-hosted AFFiNE AI can be configured with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and FAL credentials
facts.dataFormat: Local-first clients keep workspace data locally and sync to AFFiNE Cloud or the operator's server; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and persistent blob storage
facts.gapVsPaid: AFFiNE has far fewer workshop templates, facilitation controls, integrations, embedded app connectors, and enterprise administration features than Miro.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted/desktop app installs cleanly; self-hosting is a multi-service Docker deployment that needs a domain, TLS, secrets, storage, backups, and AI-provider keys for AI features

alternatives.name: CryptPad
alternatives.desc: Encrypted collaborative whiteboards with persistent folders, permissions, and sharing; fewer templates, far better data boundaries.

facts.install: Use a public CryptPad instance, or self-host the Node.js service behind a reverse proxy
facts.dataFormat: Documents are encrypted in the browser before upload; the server stores encrypted document files, blobs, and account pin metadata on its filesystem and cannot read document content
facts.gapVsPaid: CryptPad's encrypted whiteboard is much plainer and lacks Miro's facilitation toolkit, templates, integrations, voting, timers, and app marketplace.
facts.setupBlocker: Public hosting is immediate; self-hosting requires two domains or subdomains, HTTPS, strict security headers, Node.js configuration, persistent storage, and careful upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Excalidraw
alternatives.desc: The best simple escape hatch for collaborative diagrams, workshops, and planning: fast, free, local-first, and pleasantly uninterested in becoming Salesforce.

facts.install: Open the hosted web app/PWA, or deploy the static app and optional collaboration server
facts.dataFormat: Solo drawings are stored in browser storage or explicit .excalidraw JSON files; exports include PNG and SVG; multiplayer room data is end-to-end encrypted and the decryption key is carried in the share URL
facts.gapVsPaid: Excalidraw covers diagrams and simple workshops but not Miro's vast template, integration, facilitation, planning, and enterprise-governance ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the hosted app; the trade-off appears later because durable workspace organization, centralized team administration, and managed version history are deliberately minimal

alternatives.name: tldraw
alternatives.desc: A polished instant multiplayer canvas with sharing and no account requirement; lighter on facilitation, integrations, and admin.

facts.install: Open tldraw.com in a browser; no account is required for a quick canvas
facts.dataFormat: Hosted shared canvases live in tldraw's cloud; local/offline documents use browser IndexedDB, and snapshots or .tldr JSON files can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: tldraw is frictionless but has far fewer templates, integrations, planning widgets, facilitation features, and team administration controls than Miro.

alternatives.name: WBO
alternatives.desc: A tiny, durable collaborative board with persistent rooms and a free hosted instance; useful precisely because it does not try to run the company.

facts.install: Use the free hosted instance, or run the Docker image/Node.js server
facts.dataFormat: Boards are persisted as JSON files in the server's data directory; a Docker deployment must mount that directory, while public-hosted boards live on the operator's server
facts.gapVsPaid: WBO provides only the basic shared canvas and omits nearly all of Miro's workshop structure, integrations, templates, planning tools, and administration.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the public instance; self-hosting needs Docker or Node.js, a persistent writable volume with the expected user ownership, backups, and a public URL/TLS

notes: Good kinda because open-source makes the demo fast but production/workshop depth remains.
prompt:
Build me a personal whiteboard app to replace Miro. Requirements:

- Do not write a canvas engine from scratch: build on the tldraw SDK (React +
  Vite). It already does shapes, sticky notes, connectors, and selection well.
- A local web app on localhost:4900 with a board picker: named boards with
  thumbnails, create, rename, delete.
- Each board autosaves its tldraw snapshot JSON to SQLite (better-sqlite3 behind a
  small Express API) 2 seconds after the last change, keeping the previous 20
  snapshots as undo insurance.
- A toolbar button exports the current board as PNG and SVG to
  ~/Whiteboards/<board-name>.png.
- A template row on the new-board screen seeded from JSON files in templates/:
  retro grid, brainstorm columns, weekly plan.
- Works fully offline, binds to localhost, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Optional: share-with-one-person mode over my private network using tldraw's sync
  package, two cursors max. Skip it if it costs more than an hour.
- Out of scope: workshop facilitation tools (timers, voting), integrations, and
  performance tuning for 50-person boards. This is my thinking canvas, not a venue.
- README: dev and build commands, and where board data lives on disk.
